newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran oil minister defends cautious budget oil price.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil minister defends cautious budget oil price.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh on Monday fought against parliamentary moves to adopt a higher oil price in the budget for the next Iranian year which starts on March 21.

In a parliamentary debate broadcast live on Tehran radio, Aghazadeh argued against proposals made by deputies to hike the budgeted oil price by a further 50 cents a barrel above the $17.50 agreed by the government and a parliamentary commission.
"This unrealistic value that you are suggesting will make me come here next year to correct the budget...Today I can tell you I cannot do that (provide the extra oil income)," he said.

Aghazadeh stressed that Iran was already adopting the highest oil price of many of its fellow members in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) such as Saudi Arabia which had adopted a budget oil price of $16.50 and Kuwait which budgeted $16.00.

"If I am asked in OPEC what your price is based on, what should I say? Just because the price went up for a couple of months we got excited and increased the price of the barrel by a few dollars?" said the veteran oil minister.
Under the 188 trillion rial ($108 billion) budget proposed for next year, oil is Iran's biggest earner, contributing 41 percent of government revenue or 30.7 trillion rials.
World oil prices have reached their highest level since the 1990-1991 Gulf War earning Tehran -- the world's third largest oil exporter -- a windfall of $2.5 billion more than forecast.
This year's budget is based on an oil price of $15.50.

Iranian energy officials have taken a less bullish line on future oil prices and have warned that strong prices cannot be guaranteed into this year, particularly in the second quarter when world petroleum demand seasonally ebbs.

Aghazadeh also highlighted differences in the proposed budget and the country's current Five Year Plan (1995-2000) on the volume of oil exports used to base budget revenue forecasts. He said the proposed budget was based on exports of 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) compared with 2.45 million bpd in the five-year plan.
($1=1,750 rials at official rate for state budget accounts)
